headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

Below is a quick‑start guide to a few popular “IP‑to‑company” APIs that will let you feed an IP address and receive back company metadata (name, industry, size, HQ location, phone numbers, email domains, etc.). I’ve grouped them by cost tier, typical payload, and a short snippet of how to call each one in Python (using the `requests` library). Feel free to pick the one that best matches your volume, budget, and data‑quality needs. --- ## 1️⃣ Free / Low‑Cost Options (good for prototyping) | Service | Endpoint (example) | Typical Response Fields | Free Tier Limits | Notes | |---------|--------------------|------------------------|------------------|-------| | **ipinfo.io** | `https://ipinfo.io//json` | `hostname`, `city`, `region`, `country`, `loc`, `org`, `postal`, `timezone` | 50k requests/month (free plan) | Returns the ASN (`org`) but no company name; you’ll need to map ASN → company yourself (e.g., via BGPview). | | **ipapi.co** | `https://ipapi.co//json/` | `ip`, `city`, `region`, `country_name`, `country_code`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `asn`, `org` | 30k requests/day (free plan) | Same as above – ASN + org string, but no structured company data. | | **ipgeolocation.io** | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&ip=` | `ip`, `continent_name`, `country_name`, `state_prov`, `city`, `zipcode`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `isp`, `organization`, `currency`, `time_zone` | 1000 requests/day (free plan) | Provides ISP & organization strings; still not full company profile. | > **Bottom line:** These free tiers are great for getting basic geo‑location + ISP/org strings, but they don’t return structured company profiles (size, revenue, phone, email domain, etc.). For richer data you’ll need a paid plan or a dedicated business‑intelligence provider. --- ## 2️⃣ Paid / Enterprise‑Grade APIs (structured company data) | Service | Endpoint (example) | Typical Response Fields | Pricing (starting) | Notes | |---------|--------------------|------------------------|-------------------|-------| | **Clearbit Enrichment** | `https://person.clearbit.com/v2/people/find?email=`
or
`https://company.clearbit.com/v1/domains/find?domain=` | `name`, `title`, `location`, `industry`, `employees`, `founded`, `description`, `linkedin`, `twitter`, `phone`, `address`, `website` | $99/mo (10k credits) | Requires an email or domain; you can reverse‑lookup a domain from an IP’s `org` field. | | **FullContact (now Google People API)** | `https://api.fullcontact.com/v3/person.enrich` | `fullName`, `emails`, `phones`, `addresses`, `socialProfiles`, `company`, `jobTitle`, `avatarUrl` | $49/mo (10k contacts) | Similar to Clearbit; you’ll need to supply an email or domain. | | **Hunter.io Domain Search** | `https://api.hunter.io/v2/domain-search?domain=&api_key=YOUR_KEY` | `domain`, `open_positions`, `company`, `size`, `industry`, `location`, `revenue`, `employees`, `founder`, `founding_year`, `linkedin_company_id` | $399/mo (5000 emails) | Focuses on email patterns & company info. | | **ZoomInfo (via ZoomInfo API)** | `https://api.zoominfo.com/v1/company?domain=` | `companyId`, `name`, `industry`, `size`, `annualRevenue`, `phone`, `address`, `linkedin`, `facebook`, `twitter`, `description` | Custom pricing (starts ~ $2000/mo) | Enterprise‑grade; requires a contract. | | **Datanyze** | `https://api.datanyze.com/v1/company?domain=` | `companyId`, `name`, `industry`, `size`, `annualRevenue`, `phone`, `address`, `linkedin`, `twitter`, `description` | Custom pricing | Good for tech stack insights. | | **Crunchbase API** | `https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations/?user_key=YOUR_KEY` | `name`, `homepage_url`, `description`, `category_list`, `funding_total`, `num_employees_min`, `num_employees_max`, `year_founded`, `location_city`, `location_country`, `logo_image_url` | $299/mo (10k queries) | Crunchbase offers a rich dataset but you’ll need to map IP→Crunchbase ID first. | > **How to use:** > 1. Resolve the IP to a domain or organization string (via `ipinfo.io` or similar). > 2. Pass that domain to the enrichment API. > 3. Parse the returned JSON for fields like `company.name`, `company.industry`, `company.phone`, `company.address`. --- ## 3️⃣ Example Workflow (Python) Below is a minimal end‑to‑end example that stitches together a free geolocation lookup with a paid enrichment step. Replace placeholders with your actual API keys. ```python import requests def get_ip_info(ip, api_key=None): """Return basic IP metadata (free tier).""" url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json" resp = requests.get(url, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() return resp.json() def enrich_domain(domain, clearbit_key): """Return enriched company data from Clearbit.""" url = f"https://company.clearbit.com/v1/domains/find?domain={domain}" headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {clearbit_key}"} resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() return resp.json() def main(): # 1️⃣ Basic IP lookup ip = "8.8.8.8" ip_data = get_ip_info(ip) print("IP Info:", ip_data) # 2️⃣ Extract domain or org string org_str = ip_data.get("org", "") # e.g., "AS15169 Google LLC" # Try to pull out the domain part (simple heuristic) domain = None if "." in org_str: parts = org_str.split() for p in parts: if "." in p: domain = p.strip(".") break if not domain: print("Could not extract a domain from org string.") return # 3️⃣ Enrich the domain clearbit_key = "YOUR_CLEARBIT_API_KEY" try: enriched = enrich_domain(domain, clearbit_key) print("\nEnriched Company Data:") print(f"Name: {enriched['name']}") print(f"Industry: {enriched['industry']}") print(f"Phone: {enriched.get('phone', 'N/A')}") print(f"Address: {enriched.get('address', {}).get('street', '')}, " f"{enriched.get('address', {}).get('city', '')}, " f"{enriched.get('address', {}).get('country', '')}") except requests.HTTPError as err: print(f"Enrichment failed: {err}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ### What the script does 1. Calls `ipinfo.io` to get the ASN/organization string for the IP. 2. Heuristically extracts a domain from that string (you may need a more robust parser depending on your data). 3. Calls Clearbit’s domain enrichment endpoint to fetch structured company data. Feel free to swap `enrich_domain()` for another provider’s endpoint (e.g., Hunter.io, ZoomInfo) – the pattern is the same: make a GET request with your API key in the header or query string, then parse the JSON. --- ## 4️⃣ Things to Keep in Mind | Topic | Why it matters | Practical tip | |-------|----------------|---------------| | **Rate limits** | Exceeding limits can throttle or ban your IP. | Use exponential backoff; cache responses locally. | | **Privacy & compliance** | Some jurisdictions restrict collecting personal/company data. | Verify that your use case complies with GDPR, CCPA, etc. | | **Data freshness** | Company info changes frequently. | Store timestamps; re‑query periodically if you need up‑to‑date data. | | **Domain extraction** | Not all IPs belong to a single domain; corporate networks may host multiple sites. | Consider reverse DNS lookups (`dig -x `) or WHOIS lookups for better accuracy. | | **Multiple providers** | Each provider has strengths (e.g., Crunchbase for funding, ZoomInfo for sales leads). | Layer providers: start with a cheap one for bulk enrichment, then hit a premium one for high‑value targets. | --- ## 5️⃣ Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Provider | Key Endpoint | Auth Method | Typical Cost | |----------|--------------|-------------|--------------| | **ipinfo.io** | `/ip//json` | API key in query param | $5/mo (25k req/day) | | **ipapi.co** | `/ip//json/` | API key in header | $9/mo (30k req/day) | | **Clearbit** | `/v2/companies/find?domain=` | Bearer token in header | $99/mo (10k credits) | | **Hunter.io** | `/v2/domain-search?domain=` | API key in query param | $399/mo (5k emails) | | **ZoomInfo** | `/v1/company?domain=` | OAuth2 bearer token | Custom (enterprise) | | **Crunchbase** | `/v3.1/organizations/` | User key in query param | $299/mo (10k queries) | --- ### Final Thought If you’re building a product that needs to surface company data for arbitrary IP addresses, the most common architecture is: 1. **Free tier** → Resolve IP → Get ASN/org string. 2. **Paid tier** → Map org string → Domain → Enrich domain → Return structured company record. This two‑step approach keeps costs down while still giving you the richer data you need for lead generation, fraud detection, or market research. Happy coding!
